appellations.summary: A small Vino de Calidad in northern Segovia, just south of Ribera del Duero along the Duratón, with vineyards up to 900 m. Only about 70 hectares and a few producers.
appellations.terroir: High, cold limestone plateau.
appellations.nerd_note: Its villages sit along the Duratón gorge, a natural park famous for griffon vultures.

appellations.name: Sierra de Salamanca
appellations.grapes: Rufete (local), Tempranillo, Garnacha; Viura, Moscatel
appellations.summary: In the Sierra de Francia, south of Salamanca, terraced vineyards of granite and slate around Mogarraz and San Esteban de la Sierra grow Rufete, a fragile, fragrant local red that makes light, Pinot-like wines. About 130 hectares.
appellations.terroir: Mountain terraces at 400 to 1,000 m with a wetter Atlantic-influenced climate.
appellations.nerd_note: Rufete is also grown in Portugal's Dão and Douro as Tinta Pinheira.

appellations.name: Cebreros
appellations.grapes: Garnacha, Albillo Real
appellations.summary: Cebreros, in the province of Ávila on the northern slopes of the Sierra de Gredos, is part of the Gredos Garnacha revival. Old bush vines of Garnacha at 700 to 1,100 m on granite and slate give fine, perfumed reds, and Albillo Real fresh whites. Producers like Rafael Mancebo, Daniel Landi and the Comando G team helped bring attention.
appellations.terroir: Granite and slate slopes, with a continental mountain climate.
appellations.nerd_note: Before the Gredos revival, Cebreros supplied bulk Garnacha to Madrid's taverns.

appellations.name: Abadía Retuerta
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo (about three-quarters), Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Petit Verdot, Merlot; whites from Albillo Mayor, Sauvignon Blanc, Godello, Verdejo
appellations.summary: A Vino de Pago at Sardón de Duero, just west of the Ribera del Duero boundary, around the 12th-century abbey of Santa María de Retuerta. The estate covers 700 hectares with about 180 hectares of vines. Its wines were long sold as Vino de la Tierra de Castilla y León, and in 2022 it became the 23rd Vino de Pago.
appellations.terroir: Alluvial terraces and slopes along the Duero, with sandy and stony soils.
appellations.nerd_note: The monastery, founded in 1146, now houses a hotel with a Michelin-starred restaurant in its old refectory.

appellations.name: Dehesa Peñalba
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: A Vino de Pago in the municipality of Villabáñez (Valladolid), on the south bank of the Duero west of Ribera, named after Peñalba de Duero, a long-abandoned village. Approved by the EU in February 2022 for red wines only, from Tempranillo, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot on warm, sandy, gravelly soils.
appellations.terroir: Warm, sandy, gravelly, well-drained soils.
appellations.nerd_note: One of three single-estate pagos in Castilla y León, all approved between 2021 and 2022.

appellations.name: Urueña
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah
appellations.summary: A Vino de Pago just north of the walled hilltop town of Urueña in western Valladolid, made by Heredad de Urueña, the only producer. Registered by the EU in November 2021.
appellations.terroir: Limestone plateau at about 800 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Urueña is also Spain's 'Villa del Libro', a town of bookshops inside medieval walls.

appellations.name: Rías Baixas
appellations.grapes: Albariño (about 95%), Loureiro, Treixadura, Caíño Blanco, Torrontés, Godello; reds Caíño Tinto, Espadeiro, Sousón, Mencía, Brancellao, Loureiro Tinto
appellations.summary:
Rías Baixas is Spain's Atlantic white-wine capital, named after the drowned river valleys (*rías*) that cut into Galicia's southwest coast. Albariño, a thick-skinned, aromatic grape that stands up to rain, makes nearly all its wine: peach, citrus, white flowers and a salty, sea-air finish. The DO was founded in 1988 and now has about 4,600 hectares, divided into more than 20,000 tiny plots, and around 180 wineries. It sold almost 29 million litres in 2023/24, one of the five most valuable DOs in Spain.

The best wines are increasingly long-lived: lees-aged Albariño from Pazo de Señorans, Do Ferreiro, Zárate, Forjas del Salnés and Rodrigo Méndez can age for a decade or more, and old ungrafted vines survive in sandy coastal plots. The traditional trellis, the *parra*, is a pergola of granite posts and wires that lifts the canopy two metres above the ground for air.
appellations.terroir: Five subzones: Val do Salnés (the coolest, wettest and the historic home of Albariño, around Cambados), Condado do Tea (warmer, inland along the Miño, with Treixadura and Loureiro in blends), O Rosal (at the Miño's mouth, with terraces and blends with Loureiro and Caíño), Soutomaior (a tiny zone near Pontevedra) and Ribeira do Ulla (in the north, inland from Padrón). Soils are mostly granite-based sandy loams, acidic and free-draining; rainfall is 1,600 mm on the coast.
appellations.nerd_note: Albariño's Salnés stronghold has vines planted more than two centuries ago: Do Ferreiro's Cepas Vellas comes from a vineyard said to be over 200 years old, ungrafted on sandy soil.

appellations.name: Ribeiro
appellations.grapes: Treixadura, Torrontés, Godello, Loureiro, Albariño, Lado, Caíño Blanco; reds Caíño, Sousón, Brancellao, Ferrón, Mencía
appellations.summary: Ribeiro, in the valleys of the Miño, Avia and Arnoia around Ribadavia, was Galicia's great medieval wine export, shipped to England in the 14th century and celebrated in the Golden Age. Today it is a small DO (about 1,270 hectares) and a place of quiet revival: Treixadura blends with Albariño, Loureiro and Godello make fresh, fragrant whites, and producers such as Emilio Rojo, Coto de Gomariz, Luis Anxo Rodríguez and Viña Meín are bringing back old vineyards and rare grapes. Ribeiro also makes *tostado*, a sweet wine of grapes dried on straw mats.
appellations.terroir: Terraces and slopes above three rivers at 75 to 400 m, mostly granite with sand, warmer and drier than the coast.
appellations.nerd_note: Ribeiro's medieval wine trade was controlled from Ribadavia's Jewish quarter, and the town still holds a Festa da Istoria commemorating it.

appellations.name: Ribeira Sacra
appellations.grapes: Mencía, Merenzao, Brancellao, Sousón, Caíño Tinto, Garnacha Tintorera; whites Godello, Albariño, Treixadura, Dona Branca
appellations.summary:
Ribeira Sacra, the 'sacred riverbank', takes its name from the Romanesque monasteries hidden in the forests of the Sil and Miño canyons. Its vineyards are among the most dramatic on earth: narrow stone terraces (*socalcos*) on slopes of up to 100 percent gradient, many of them first cut in Roman times, so steep that grapes are harvested by hand and hauled up in boxes on rails. This is *viticultura heroica*.

The red wines, mostly Mencía with Merenzao, Brancellao and Sousón, are light, perfumed and mineral, with a slate edge. The DO dates from 1996; it has about 1,300 hectares, nearly 100 wineries, and some of Spain's most talked-about producers, including Algueira, Guímaro, Dominio do Bibei, Envínate, Fazenda Prádio and Adega Vella.
appellations.terroir: Five subzones: Amandi (the warmest, on the Sil's sunny north bank near Sober, with the steepest terraces), Chantada (the Miño around Belesar, cooler), Quiroga-Bibei (the upper Sil and Bibei, warmer, drier, with slate and Mediterranean scrub), Ribeiras do Miño and Ribeiras do Sil. Soils are slate, schist and granite; summer heat in the canyons ripens Mencía well despite Galicia's rain.
appellations.nerd_note: Ribeira Sacra has been pursuing UNESCO World Heritage status as a cultural landscape of Roman and monastic terraces; local legend says Amandi's wine was sent to Rome for the emperors.

appellations.name: Valdeorras
appellations.grapes: Godello (signature), Doña Blanca, Palomino; Mencía, Merenzao, Sousón, Garnacha Tintorera
appellations.summary: Valdeorras, the 'valley of gold' on the upper Sil in eastern Ourense, is the birthplace of the Godello revival. In the 1970s a group of local growers, Horacio Fernández among them, propagated Godello from a few surviving vines in a recovery project known as REVIVAL, and today it is one of Spain's finest white grapes: textured, citrus, saline, ageworthy. Rafael Palacios (brother of Álvaro) moved to O Bolo in 2004 and his As Sortes and O Soro are benchmarks; Telmo Rodríguez's Gaba do Xil and Valdesil also show the region.
appellations.terroir: Slate and granite slopes at 300 to 700 m, with a mixed Atlantic and continental climate; the higher, eastern sector (O Bolo, Larouco) is particularly cool.
appellations.nerd_note: The Romans mined gold in the Sil, hence the valley's name; Godeval's winery in O Barco is housed in the 12th-century Xagoaza monastery.

appellations.name: Monterrei
appellations.grapes: Doña Blanca, Godello, Treixadura; Mencía, Merenzao, Arauxa (Tempranillo)
appellations.summary: Monterrei, around Verín on the Portuguese border, is Galicia's warmest and most continental DO, sitting in a valley shared with Portugal's Chaves. It makes fresh Godello, Treixadura and Doña Blanca whites and Mencía reds, with producers like Quinta da Muradella reviving old field blends. About 800 hectares.
appellations.terroir: Valley and slopes at 350 to 900 m, with granite and slate soils and hot dry summers.
appellations.nerd_note: The fortress of Monterrei, above Verín, was the region's royal frontier castle; vineyards of Valle de Monterrei and Ladera de Monterrei are its two subzones.

appellations.name: Bierzo
appellations.grapes: Mencía (about 70% of grapes), Garnacha Tintorera, Merenzao, Estaladiña; Godello, Doña Blanca, Palomino
appellations.summary:
Bierzo is Spain's Mencía capital, a mountain basin in León where Galicia's Atlantic influence meets the Castilian plateau. Its best wines, from old vineyards on steep slate slopes, have the floral, peppery and mineral freshness that made Mencía fashionable worldwide. The arrival of Álvaro Palacios and his nephew Ricardo Pérez in 1999 (Descendientes de J. Palacios, in Corullón) and the work of native son Raúl Pérez, together with Losada, Dominio de Tares and Castro Ventosa, turned a region of cooperatives into one of the most dynamic in Spain.

Bierzo's 2019 classification was a revolution: wines can be Vino de Villa (one village), Vino de Paraje (a named site), Vino de Viña Clasificada and Gran Vino de Viña Clasificada, each with progressively lower yields. The first village and paraje wines reached shops in June 2020. Mencía makes up three-quarters of the old plantings; Godello is the main white.
appellations.terroir: A sheltered basin at 450 to 900 m surrounded by mountains, with clay soils on the valley floor and slate and quartzite on the slopes. About 700 mm of rain, warmer than Galicia's coast.
appellations.nerd_note: Bierzo's parajes were defined using the Spanish land registry, and its controls require 100 percent of the grapes from the named place, stricter than the EU's 85 percent rule.

appellations.name: Cangas
appellations.grapes: Albarín Negro, Carrasquín, Verdejo Negro, Mencía; Albarín Blanco
appellations.summary: A tiny Vino de Calidad around Cangas del Narcea, in Asturias, with about 60 hectares on steep slate slopes and eight wineries. Its native varieties, Carrasquín and Albarín Negro, give light, peppery reds with high acidity.
appellations.terroir: Slopes at 400 to 900 m above the Narcea, cool and wet.
appellations.nerd_note: Asturias's only wine designation; the 11th-century Corias monastery nearby is now a Parador.

appellations.name: Getariako Txakolina / Chacolí de Getaria / Txakolí de Getaria
match: Getariako Txakolina / Chacolí de Getaria / Txakolí de Getaria
appellations.grapes: Hondarrabi Zuri, Hondarrabi Beltza, Gros Manseng, Petit Manseng, Petit Corbu
appellations.summary: The most famous Txakoli, from the fishing town of Getaria and the Gipuzkoa coast near San Sebastián. Its wines are bright, lightly spritzy, saline and low in alcohol (often 10.5 to 11.5 percent), the classic partner to anchovies, grilled fish and pintxos, poured from a height to raise the fizz. The DO was created in 1989 with a few dozen hectares and covers about 460 today.
appellations.terroir: Steep slopes of clay and sandstone facing the Bay of Biscay; very wet (1,600 mm), mild, windy.
appellations.nerd_note: Ameztoi's Rubentis, a pink Txakoli, became a cult wine in New York bars in the 2010s.

appellations.name: Bizkaiko Txakolina / Chacolí de Bizkaia / Txakolí de Bizkaia
match: Bizkaiko Txakolina / Chacolí de Bizkaia / Txakolí de Bizkaia
appellations.grapes: Hondarrabi Zuri, Folle Blanche (Munemahatsa), Hondarrabi Beltza, Izkiriota, Sauvignon Blanc, Riesling, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: The Txakoli of Bizkaia covers vineyards across the province, from Bakio on the coast to the Txorierri valley near Bilbao. It is a little rounder and fuller than Getaria's, with some barrel-fermented and lees-aged wines, and around 35 producers.
appellations.terroir: Wet, cool Atlantic hills with clay and marl.
appellations.nerd_note: Bizkaiko producers grow Folle Blanche, locally called Munemahatsa, the same grape once used for Cognac and Armagnac.

appellations.name: Arabako Txakolina / Txakolí de Álava / Chacolí de Álava
match: Arabako Txakolina / Txakolí de Álava / Chacolí de Álava
appellations.grapes: Hondarrabi Zuri, Gros Manseng, Petit Manseng, Petit Corbu
appellations.summary: The smallest Txakoli DO, around Amurrio and Ayala in northern Álava, inland on the Atlantic side of the province (far from Rioja Alavesa). About 100 hectares and seven wineries.
appellations.terroir: Inland valleys at 300 to 500 m, cool and wet.
appellations.nerd_note: It was revived in the 1990s after viticulture had almost vanished from the Aiara valley.

appellations.name: Navarra
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Graciano, Syrah; Chardonnay, Viura, Moscatel de Grano Menudo, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: Navarra was once synonymous with rosado: bright, strawberry-scented Garnacha made by the *sangrado* (bleeding) method, a fixture of Spanish tables. In the 1980s, guided by the EVENA research station in Olite, it pivoted to Tempranillo, Cabernet and Merlot, producing approachable reds and blends. The modern revival is about old Garnacha from the Baja Montaña and high vineyards, from producers like Domaines Lupier, Viña Zorzal and Bodegas Máximo Abete, and about delicate *rosado*. Navarra also has a sweet tradition: Chivite's Colección 125 Vendimia Tardía Moscatel.
appellations.terroir: Five subzones from cool, rainy Baja Montaña and Tierra Estella to the hot, dry Ribera Baja near Tudela, where the Bardenas Reales semi-desert begins. Soils are limestone, clay, and gravels.
appellations.nerd_note: Navarra's rosados were traditionally made by bleeding juice off the vats, the *sangrado*; the colour comes from a few hours of skin contact.

appellations.name: Pago de Arínzano
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon; Chardonnay
appellations.summary: An estate on a bend of the Ega river near Estella, with an 11th-century manor and a winery by Rafael Moneo, the first Vino de Pago outside Castilla-La Mancha. Developed by the Chivite family from 1988, it has since changed hands and is now sold as Señorío de Arínzano. Its microclimate combines Atlantic and Mediterranean influences.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and alluvial soils on the Ega, at about 450 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Its winery, a contemporary building by the Pritzker-winning architect Rafael Moneo, sits beside the restored medieval manor and chapel.

appellations.name: Pago de Otazu
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Tempranillo; Chardonnay
appellations.summary: The northernmost red-wine estate in Spain, in the Etxauri valley near Pamplona, with a 19th-century winery, a medieval palace and a contemporary art collection. Its cool climate makes Chardonnay and Bordeaux-style reds.
appellations.terroir: Gravel and clay soils in the cool valley of the Arga, where Atlantic influence is strong.
appellations.nerd_note: Otazu's barrel cellar doubles as a contemporary art gallery, and the estate has a 12th-century Romanesque church.

appellations.name: Prado de Irache
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Graciano, Mazuela, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: A small pago belonging to Bodegas Irache near Estella, next to the Monastery of Irache on the Camino de Santiago. At 15 hectares it is one of the smallest pagos in Spain.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and clay at about 500 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Bodegas Irache's free wine fountain for pilgrims on the Camino has flowed since 1991.

appellations.name: Bolandin
appellations.grapes: Garnacha, Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: Navarra's newest pago, a single estate of about 114 hectares registered in the ministry's 2026 list. As with every pago, the winery must grow, make and bottle all the wine on the estate.
appellations.terroir: Southern Navarra, in the Ebro basin.
appellations.nerd_note: Navarra now has four Vinos de Pago, more than any other region except Castilla-La Mancha and Valencia.

appellations.name: Campo de Borja
appellations.grapes: Garnacha (dominant), Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah; Macabeo, Moscatel
appellations.summary: Campo de Borja calls itself the Empire of Garnacha, and it has a claim: old vineyards of Garnacha, some more than a century old, on the slopes of the Moncayo at 350 to 700 m. The Borsao group and Alto Moncayo (a project with the Australian winemaker Chris Ringland) built an international following for dense, value Garnacha. The Cistercians of Veruela planted here in the 12th century.
appellations.terroir: Continental and dry, battered by the cold *cierzo* wind, with limestone, clay and stony soils.
appellations.nerd_note: The Cistercian monastery of Veruela, founded in 1146, now houses the DO's wine museum.

appellations.name: Calatayud
appellations.grapes: Garnacha, Tempranillo, Syrah; Macabeo, Garnacha Blanca, Moscatel
appellations.summary: Calatayud, west of Zaragoza, has some of the highest Garnacha vineyards in Spain (up to 1,000 m) on slate and quartzite slopes along the Jalón and Jiloca. Old bush vines give intense but fresh Garnacha. Producers like El Escocés Volante (Norrel Robertson) and Bodegas Ateca (Juan Gil's group) helped make its name.
appellations.terroir: Mountain slopes at 550 to 1,000 m, continental, with slate, quartzite and gypsum soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Calatayud's Garnacha Blanca and Garnacha Tinta often grow together in old field blends, and some vines are ungrafted.

appellations.name: Cariñena
appellations.grapes: Garnacha, Tempranillo, Cariñena (Mazuela), Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Merlot; Macabeo, Garnacha Blanca, Moscatel
appellations.summary: Cariñena is one of Spain's oldest DOs (named in the 1932 statute) and gave its name to the grape the French call Carignan. Paradoxically, the grape is now rare here; Garnacha and Tempranillo dominate. Large cooperatives and family wineries make value reds, and a few producers are bottling old-vine Cariñena and Garnacha, including the renewed *Vino de Calidad de Cariñena* old-vine programme.
appellations.terroir: A plateau and the foothills of the Sierra de Algairén at 400 to 800 m, with slate, limestone and red clay soils and the dry *cierzo* wind.
appellations.nerd_note: Cariñena's name travelled with the grape: Carignan in France, Mazuelo in Rioja, Samsó in Catalonia, Carignano in Sardinia.

appellations.name: Somontano
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Tempranillo, Syrah, Garnacha, Moristel, Parraleta; Chardonnay, Gewürztraminer, Macabeo
appellations.summary: Somontano, 'below the mountain', sits at the foot of the Pyrenees around Barbastro in Huesca. It is cooler than the rest of Aragón and became the poster child for international varieties in the 1990s: Chardonnay, Gewürztraminer, Cabernet. Local grapes Moristel and Parraleta are coming back. Enate, Viñas del Vero and Blecua are the leading names.
appellations.terroir: Foothills at 350 to 650 m, with limestone and clay soils and a continental climate cooled by mountain air.
appellations.nerd_note: Enate commissions artists like Antoni Tàpies and Eduardo Chillida for its labels and has a contemporary art collection.

appellations.name: Aylés
appellations.grapes: Garnacha, Tempranillo, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: Aragón's first Vino de Pago, the estate of Señorío de Aylés near Mezalocha, south of Zaragoza, around a historic farm on the edge of the Cariñena country. It makes Garnacha-led reds and rosados.
appellations.terroir: Clay, limestone and gravel at about 500 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Aylés was registered as a pago in 2010 and by the EU in 2011, the first of two in Aragón.

appellations.name: Urbezo
appellations.grapes: Garnacha, Cabernet Sauvignon, Mazuela, Merlot, Syrah, Tempranillo; Chardonnay, Garnacha Blanca, Moscatel de Alejandría
appellations.summary: Registered by the EU in October 2024 as Spain's 26th Vino de Pago and Aragón's second, Urbezo covers just over 230 hectares in Cariñena on the slopes of the Sierra de Algairén at about 490 m. The application was filed in 2019 by the estate's winery (Solar de Urbezo).
appellations.terroir: Foothills of the Sierra de Algairén, slate and clay soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Spain's ministry list files Urbezo under the DO term rather than VP, but the ministry's own announcement calls it a vino de pago.

appellations.name: Priorat / Priorato
appellations.grapes: Garnatxa, Samsó (Cariñena), Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Merlot; Garnatxa Blanca, Macabeu, Pedro Ximénez
appellations.summary:
Priorat is Spain's most dramatic red-wine region and one of only two DOCa (in Catalan, DOQ) appellations. Its 2,200 hectares of vines grow on llicorella, a dark slate and quartzite that splits into flakes and forces roots deep for water; the yields from old Garnatxa and Samsó bush vines can fall below 1 kg per plant. The wines are powerful but, at their best, also fresh, with a mineral, graphite and dark-herb character and enormous ageing potential.

The modern legend began in 1989 with the 'Gang of Five' in Gratallops; Álvaro Palacios's L'Ermita, first made in 1993, became Spain's most expensive wine. Today some 115 wineries work here, from cooperatives that kept old vines alive to small producers like Terroir al Límit, Mas Doix, Ferrer Bobet, Clos Figueras and Mas Martinet. Since 2017 the region has a village and paratge system and its own Gran Vinya Classificada, Spain's equivalent of grand cru: L'Ermita, Mas de la Rosa and Tossal d'en Bou were listed in 2024.
appellations.terroir: Llicorella slate and quartzite on steep slopes and terraces at 100 to 750 m, sheltered by the Montsant cliffs. A Mediterranean climate made continental by altitude, 400 to 600 mm of rain, and heat moderated by cool nights.
appellations.nerd_note: Grape yields for Gran Vinya Classificada are capped at 3,000 kg/ha for reds, but the old vines of L'Ermita, on a steep north-east-facing slope of llicorella, give far less.

appellations.name: Montsant
appellations.grapes: Garnatxa, Samsó (Cariñena), Ull de Llebre, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot; Garnatxa Blanca, Macabeu
appellations.summary: Montsant wraps around Priorat like a horseshoe, and until 2001 it was the Falset subzone of DO Tarragona. It shares Priorat's Garnatxa and Samsó but on more varied soils: limestone, clay, granite, and only patches of slate. Wines are generally lighter and better value, and the region has many old vines. Leading names include Capçanes (whose cooperative makes Spain's best-known kosher wine), Acústic, Joan d'Anguera, Venus La Universal and Celler Laurona.
appellations.terroir: Mostly 200 to 700 m on clay-limestone, granite, sand and some slate; Mediterranean climate.
appellations.nerd_note: Falset's 1919 cooperative winery, by Cèsar Martinell, was one of the first 'cathedrals of wine' of Catalan modernisme.

appellations.name: Terra Alta
appellations.grapes: Garnatxa Blanca (signature), Macabeu, Parellada; Garnatxa, Samsó, Garnatxa Peluda, Syrah
appellations.summary: Terra Alta, the high land in the far southwest of Catalonia, is the world's great stronghold of Garnatxa Blanca, which here gives broad, herbal, saline whites. The DO recognises a *Terra Alta Garnatxa Blanca* label for wines made only from it. Reds of Garnatxa and Garnatxa Peluda (a hairy-leaved form) are also good. The region was a Civil War battlefield in 1938 (the Battle of the Ebro), and its modernist cooperative wineries in Gandesa and El Pinell de Brai are monuments.
appellations.terroir: Plateau and hills at 350 to 600 m, with chalky clay soils, a continental-Mediterranean climate, and two winds, the dry *cerç* from the north and the humid *garbinada* from the sea.
appellations.nerd_note: Terra Alta's cooperative at El Pinell de Brai has a ceramic frieze about wine and agriculture by Xavier Nogués on its modernist facade.

appellations.name: Conca de Barberà
appellations.grapes: Trepat (native), Garnatxa, Ull de Llebre, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot; Macabeu, Parellada, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: A basin in inland Tarragona around Montblanc and the Cistercian monastery of Poblet, Conca de Barberà is home to Trepat, a light, spicy red grape used for rosado and pink Cava and now for elegant reds. It also supplies Parellada to Cava, and is the site of Torres's Milmanda Chardonnay and Grans Muralles from the castle walls at Poblet.
appellations.terroir: A sheltered valley at 350 to 600 m, cooler than the coast, with limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Poblet, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and royal pantheon of the kings of Aragón, still has monks and still makes wine.

appellations.name: Tarragona
appellations.grapes: Garnatxa, Samsó, Ull de Llebre, Cabernet, Merlot, Syrah; Macabeu, Xarel·lo, Parellada, Garnatxa Blanca, Moscatel
appellations.summary: One of Spain's historic DOs, around the Roman capital Tarraco, Tarragona once made sweet altar wine (*vi de missa*) and long-aged fortified *Tarragona Clásico*. Today it is mostly a source of everyday reds and whites in two subzones, Camp de Tarragona and Ribera d'Ebre. Reus was the hub of the 19th-century wine and brandy trade.
appellations.terroir: Coastal plain and hills (Camp de Tarragona) and the warmer Ebro valley (Ribera d'Ebre), on limestone and alluvial soils.
appellations.nerd_note: De Muller, founded in 1851, was a supplier of altar wine to the Vatican and still keeps soleras of rancio and sweet wines started in the 19th century.

appellations.name: Costers del Segre
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Garnatxa, Syrah; Macabeu, Xarel·lo, Parellada, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: An interior DO in the province of Lleida with seven subzones (Artesa, Garrigues, Pallars Jussà, Raimat, Segrià, Valls del Riu Corb and Urgell), from dry plains to pre-Pyrenean slopes. Its story begins at Raimat, where Manuel Raventós of Codorníu bought desert land in 1914, irrigated it from the Urgell canal and planted vines and pines. Castell del Remei is the other historic name.
appellations.terroir: Continental, dry (300 to 400 mm of rain) and cold-wintered, on limestone and gravel; irrigation is allowed and common.
appellations.nerd_note: Raimat's 1918 winery, by Gaudí's disciple Joan Rubió i Bellver, was among the first in Spain built in reinforced concrete.

appellations.name: Empordà
appellations.grapes: Garnatxa, Samsó (Carinyena), Cabernet, Merlot, Syrah; Garnatxa Blanca, Garnatxa Roja (Grisa), Macabeu, Moscatell
appellations.summary: Empordà, in the far northeast against the French border and the Costa Brava, was where the Greeks of Empúries landed in the 6th century BC. The tramuntana wind, which can blow for days, keeps vines healthy. Its best wines include old-vine Garnatxa and Carinyena reds and the sweet, rancio-like *Garnatxa de l'Empordà*, aged in barrels and glass demijohns in the sun.
appellations.terroir: From the Albera foothills to the Cap de Creus terraces; granite and slate in the north, alluvium and clay in the south.
appellations.nerd_note: Phylloxera reached Spain through Empordà in 1879, crossing from France; the terraces of Cap de Creus were abandoned and are now being replanted.

appellations.name: Alella
appellations.grapes: Pansa Blanca (local Xarel·lo), Garnatxa Blanca, Macabeu, Chardonnay; Garnatxa, Ull de Llebre, Cabernet, Merlot
appellations.summary: One of Spain's smallest DOs, squeezed between Barcelona's suburbs and the Maresme coast, Alella has made wine since Roman Laietania. Its granite sand soils (*sauló*) suit Pansa Blanca, the local Xarel·lo. Urban sprawl has shrunk it, but Alta Alella and a few others keep it alive, and Alta Alella's Vallcirera site is a Cava de Paraje Calificado.
appellations.terroir: Granite sand (sauló) slopes facing the sea, warm and humid.
appellations.nerd_note: The Alella Vinícola cooperative building of 1906 is another of Catalonia's modernist wine monuments.

appellations.name: Pla de Bages
appellations.grapes: Picapoll (local white), Macabeu, Chardonnay; Sumoll, Mandó, Ull de Llebre, Merlot, Cabernet, Garnatxa
appellations.summary: Around Manresa, in the centre of Catalonia, Pla de Bages was a huge vineyard in the 19th century until phylloxera. Its symbols are the *tines*, round stone vats built in the vineyards to ferment wine on the spot, and Picapoll, a fresh, fragrant white. Abadal and Artium (a cooperative of Artés) lead the revival.
appellations.terroir: Plateau at 400 to 600 m, cooler and continental, on sandstone and clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Hundreds of stone *tines* survive in the vineyards and woods of the Bages, some restored as heritage sites.

appellations.name: Penedès
appellations.grapes: Xarel·lo, Macabeu, Parellada, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Malvasia de Sitges; Ull de Llebre, Garnatxa, Cabernet, Merlot, Sumoll
appellations.summary:
DO Penedès is the still and sparkling-wine DO of the region that is the heart of Cava. It has just over 13,000 registered hectares, of which only around 5,000 are used for Penedès wines; the rest goes to Cava. Since the 2025 harvest, all grapes and wines under the DO must be certified organic, a world first. Xarel·lo is the star: structured, herbal and ageworthy, as still wine or sparkling. *Clàssic Penedès*, the DO's own traditional-method sparkling category created in the early 2010s, requires organic grapes from Penedès and long lees ageing (at least 15 months).

The region also has a history of international varieties: Jean Leon planted Cabernet and Chardonnay in 1963 and Torres's Gran Coronas Black Label 1970 (today Mas La Plana) beat top Bordeaux at the 1979 Gault-Millau Wine Olympiad.
appellations.terroir: From the Garraf coast to the Alt Penedès hills (up to about 800 m), limestone and clay soils; Mediterranean climate.
appellations.nerd_note: Malvasia de Sitges, a sweet wine from the coastal town, is kept alive by the town's hospital, which has owned its historic vineyard since the 1930s.

appellations.name: Cava
appellations.grapes: Macabeu (Viura), Xarel·lo, Parellada, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Garnacha, Monastrell, Trepat, Subirat Parent (Malvasía)
appellations.summary:
Cava is Spain's traditional-method sparkling wine, made since Josep Raventós's first bottles at Codorníu in 1872, and it is unusual in being defined as much by method as by place: its 157 municipalities are scattered across Catalonia, Aragón, Navarra, La Rioja, the Basque Country, Valencia and Extremadura, though the great majority comes from Catalonia, above all the Penedès. With 37,500 hectares and some 340 producers, it sells around 240 million bottles a year, one of the world's largest sparkling-wine appellations after Champagne and Prosecco.

The 2020 reform split Cava in two: *Cava de Guarda*, with at least 9 months on lees, and *Cava de Guarda Superior*, which includes Reserva (18 months), Gran Reserva (30 months) and Paraje Calificado (36 months), and from the 2025 harvest must be organic. It also introduced zones and subzones: Comtats de Barcelona (with Valls d'Anoia-Foix, Serra de Mar, Conca del Gaià, Serra de Prades and Pla de Ponent), Valle del Ebro (Alto Ebro and Altiplano de Cariñena), Viñedos de Almendralejo and Levante (Requena). At the top, *Cava de Paraje Calificado* requires a single estate, vines over 10 years old, yields up to 8,000 kg/ha, hand harvesting, estate vinification, vintage dating and 36 months on lees: 15 wines from eight producers in 2026.

Despite these reforms, some of the best growers left. Raventós i Blanc departed in 2012 to create its Conca del Riu Anoia label. Gramona, Recaredo, Llopart, Torelló, Nadal, Sabaté i Coca and others had launched Corpinnat as a collective brand inside Cava, then left the DO in 2019 to sell organic, hand-harvested, estate-made Penedès sparkling wine under that name alone. By 2026 Corpinnat had 21 members selling about three million bottles a year.
appellations.terroir: Mostly the Penedès's limestone and clay soils and Mediterranean climate; also Requena's high plateau and Almendralejo's warm plains.
appellations.nerd_note: The Cavas de Paraje Calificado of 2026: Alta Alella's Vallcirera, Carles Andreu's Celdoni, Codorníu's La Fideuera, La Pleta and El Tros Nou, Ferrer Wines' Can Sala, Juvé & Camps's La Capella, Pere Ventura's Can Bas, Sumarroca's Cols, Peretes and Rosendo, and Vins El Cep's Can Prats.

appellations.name: Cataluña / Catalunya
appellations.grapes: Most Catalan varieties plus international grapes
appellations.summary: A regional DO created in 1999 that covers almost every vineyard in Catalonia, letting producers blend across DOs. Large firms like Torres (Sangre de Toro, Viña Sol) use it, and so do small growers working outside their local DO. About 35,500 hectares and 179 wineries.
appellations.terroir: All of Catalonia's climates and soils.
appellations.nerd_note: DO Catalunya's creation helps explain the fall of DO Penedès's sales, from about 50 million bottles to 15 million, as firms moved their brands.

appellations.name: La Mancha
appellations.grapes: Airén, Tempranillo (Cencibel), Garnacha, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Merlot, Petit Verdot; Macabeo, Verdejo, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: La Mancha is the largest DO in Spain and one of the largest delimited wine regions in the world, with about 147,000 registered hectares across 190 municipalities in Ciudad Real, Cuenca, Toledo and Albacete. Only a fraction of the vineyard's harvest is bottled under the DO; most goes to bulk wine, brandy and grape concentrate. Its historic grape is Airén, a hardy white that gives neutral wine, but the region is now dominated by Tempranillo and international varieties. Quality has risen sharply with modern cooperatives and estates, and the DO makes reliable, low-priced reds and whites.
appellations.terroir: A huge, flat plateau at 600 to 750 m with hot summers, cold winters and about 300 to 400 mm of rain; red clay and limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Tomelloso, the region's wine and brandy town, sits on thousands of underground *cuevas* dug to keep wine cool in huge earthenware *tinajas*.

appellations.name: Valdepeñas
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo (Cencibel), Garnacha, Cabernet Sauvignon; Airén, Macabeo
appellations.summary: Valdepeñas, an enclave inside La Mancha in the south of Ciudad Real, has been Madrid's tavern wine for centuries, aged in *tinajas* and later in American oak. The DO, one of the first named in 1932, has about 12,000 hectares but only a dozen bottlers, among them Félix Solís, one of Spain's largest wine companies. Its soft, oaky Cencibel reservas and gran reservas are among the best values in Spanish wine.
appellations.terroir: Plateau at about 700 m, with red clay over limestone and very hot summers.
appellations.nerd_note: Valdepeñas's name means 'valley of stones', and its old wineries still hold rows of earthenware tinajas taller than a person.

appellations.name: Manchuela
appellations.grapes: Bobal, Tempranillo, Garnacha, Monastrell, Syrah, Garnacha Tintorera; Macabeo, Albillo, Moscatel
appellations.summary: Between La Mancha and the Valencian border, Manchuela lies on a plateau at 600 to 1,000 m along the Júcar and Cabriel rivers. Bobal is its strength, and the DO's revival owes a lot to Finca Sandoval, founded by the wine writer Víctor de la Serna, and to Juan Antonio Ponce's natural Bobals.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and clay plateau, continental with Mediterranean influence from the east.
appellations.nerd_note: Juan Antonio Ponce, who trained with Telmo Rodríguez, ferments old-vine Bobal with whole bunches like a Beaujolais grower.

appellations.name: Méntrida
appellations.grapes: Garnacha, Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah; Albillo Real, Macabeo
appellations.summary: Méntrida, in northern Toledo where the plains meet the Sierra de Gredos, was long a bulk Garnacha supplier for Madrid. Since the 2000s the Jiménez-Landi family and others have shown its old Garnacha on granite can be fine and perfumed.
appellations.terroir: Sandy granite soils (from Gredos) and clay, at 400 to 800 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Méntrida's best vineyards rise toward the Sierra de Gredos in villages like Hormigos and El Real de San Vicente.

appellations.name: Mondéjar
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Garnacha; Malvar, Macabeo, Torrontés
appellations.summary: A small DO in southwest Guadalajara, near the Tagus, with about 360 hectares and two active wineries. Its main white grape is the local Malvar.
appellations.terroir: Plateau and hills at 700 to 800 m, limestone and clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Malvar, Mondéjar's white grape, is shared with the Madrid DO next door and is almost unknown elsewhere.

appellations.name: Ribera del Júcar
appellations.grapes: Bobal, Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Merlot; Moscatel, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: Ribera del Júcar covers seven municipalities in southern Cuenca along the Júcar river, with about 6,500 registered hectares but only nine bottling wineries in 2023/24, so most of its grapes go to cooperatives and bulk wine. Its bottled reds rely on Bobal and Tempranillo grown on stony limestone at about 700 m.
appellations.terroir: Plateau at about 700 m with stony limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: One of the smallest numbers of active wineries for its size in Spain, with only nine registered in 2023/24.

appellations.name: Uclés
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Garnacha; Verdejo, Moscatel, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: Uclés, in northwest Cuenca and eastern Toledo around the Monastery of Uclés, the 'El Escorial of La Mancha', is a small DO in the hills of the Sierra de Altomira, cooler than the plain.
appellations.terroir: Hills at 600 to 1,200 m with limestone and clay.
appellations.nerd_note: Uclés's huge monastery was the headquarters of the Order of Santiago from the 12th century.

appellations.name: Almansa
appellations.grapes: Garnacha Tintorera (signature), Monastrell, Tempranillo, Syrah; Verdejo, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: Almansa, in eastern Albacete on the edge of Valencia and Murcia, is known for Garnacha Tintorera (Alicante Bouschet), a red-fleshed grape that gives very dark wines, often blended with Monastrell. Bodegas Atalaya, of the Gil family, made it known.
appellations.terroir: Plateau at 700 to 1,000 m, with limestone and continental Mediterranean climate.
appellations.nerd_note: Garnacha Tintorera, one of the few grapes with red flesh, was bred in France in the 1860s.

appellations.name: Campo de Calatrava
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Bobal, Petit Verdot, Garnacha Tintorera; Airén, Macabeo, Verdejo, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: Spain's newest DO, registered by the EU in February 2024 as the 102nd Spanish DOP: 16 municipalities in Ciudad Real province, in the area around Almagro and the Ciudad Real plain. It covers a field of extinct volcanoes, the most significant recent volcanic area of the Iberian Peninsula, with soils rich in nickel.
appellations.terroir: Rolling hills at 700 to 900 m and plains at 630 to 650 m, on volcanic and limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: The Campo de Calatrava volcanic field has hundreds of small volcanoes and maars, the newest of them only a few thousand years old.

appellations.name: Jumilla
appellations.grapes: Monastrell (dominant), Garnacha Tintorera, Syrah, Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Petit Verdot; Airén, Macabeo, Malvasía
appellations.summary: Jumilla, straddling Murcia and Albacete, is the heartland of Monastrell. Its sandy, chalky soils kept phylloxera out until 1989, when the louse finally arrived and devastated the old ungrafted vineyards; replanting came with a modern turn. Today producers like Casa Castillo, whose José María Vicente makes some of Spain's most elegant Monastrell, Juan Gil, Bodegas Luzón and the cooperatives make wines that range from rich to fresh and stony.
appellations.terroir: High plateaus at 400 to 900 m, very dry (about 300 mm), with sandy, chalky limestone soils that drain freely.
appellations.nerd_note: Casa Castillo's Pie Franco comes from a parcel of ungrafted Monastrell planted in 1941 that survived the phylloxera of 1989 on sand.

appellations.name: Yecla
appellations.grapes: Monastrell, Garnacha Tintorera, Syrah, Tempranillo, Merlot, Cabernet; Airén, Macabeo, Merseguera
appellations.summary: Yecla is one of the few Spanish DOs to cover a single municipality. Its Monastrell, grown on limestone at 400 to 800 m, is led by Bodegas Castaño, whose family helped bring the region from bulk wine to bottled exports.
appellations.terroir: Plateau at 400 to 800 m with limestone soils and semi-arid climate.
appellations.nerd_note: Yecla has two subzones, Campo Arriba (higher, old vines) and Campo Abajo.

appellations.name: Bullas
appellations.grapes: Monastrell, Tempranillo, Syrah, Garnacha; Macabeo, Airén
appellations.summary: Bullas, in northwest Murcia, grows Monastrell at 400 to 900 m in the mountains of the Noroeste. Higher and cooler than Jumilla, it is a small region with a growing quality scene.
appellations.terroir: Terraced slopes with limestone and stony soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Bullas's wine museum is in a 19th-century winery, Bodega Melgares.

appellations.name: Alicante
appellations.grapes: Monastrell, Garnacha Tintorera, Tempranillo, Cabernet, Syrah; Moscatel de Alejandría, Merseguera, Macabeo
appellations.summary: Alicante has two subzones: Vinalopó, the inland valleys around Villena, Monòver and Pinoso, where Monastrell grows at 400 to 600 m, and the Marina Alta on the coast near Dénia, home of Moscatel. Its jewel is *Fondillón*, a legendary wine from overripe Monastrell aged at least ten years in oak, often in old soleras, which was once traded across European courts and is said to have been carried on Magellan's circumnavigation. Enrique Mendoza, Gutiérrez de la Vega and Primitivo Quiles keep the traditions.
appellations.terroir: Mediterranean coast and dry inland valleys with limestone and clay soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Fondillón is protected by name in the DO and must be made from Monastrell that is naturally overripe on the vine, without fortification.

appellations.name: Valencia
appellations.grapes: Moscatel de Alejandría, Merseguera, Macabeo, Malvasía, Pedro Ximénez; Monastrell, Garnacha Tintorera, Bobal, Tempranillo
appellations.summary: DO Valencia has four subzones: Alto Turia (high, cool whites), Valentino (central hills), Moscatel de Valencia (sweet Moscatel, often fortified, near the coast) and Clariano (south, reds). A lively group of producers including Celler del Roure (which ferments in old buried tinajas) and Rafael Cambra are reviving Mandó and Monastrell.
appellations.terroir: From coastal plain to interior hills up to 1,000 m; limestone soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Moscatel de Valencia is a *vino de licor*, often made by adding alcohol to fresh must, a style called *mistela*.

appellations.name: Utiel-Requena
appellations.grapes: Bobal (the majority), Tempranillo, Garnacha, Cabernet, Syrah; Macabeo, Tardana, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Utiel-Requena, a high plateau 70 km inland from Valencia, is the stronghold of Bobal. Long used for bulk wine and colour, Bobal is now made into fresh, dark, juicy reds and fine rosados from old bush vines. The region has about 32,000 hectares, five Vinos de Pago (El Terrerazo, Los Balagueses, Chozas Carrascal, Vera de Estenas and Tharsys) and the Levante zone of Cava. Mustiguillo's Toni Sarrión led the Bobal revival in the late 1990s.
appellations.terroir: Plateau at 600 to 900 m, continental, with limestone and clay soils and frosts.
appellations.nerd_note: Bobal's name is usually traced to Latin *bovale*, for the bull's-head shape of its bunches.

appellations.name: Vinos de Madrid
appellations.grapes: Garnacha, Tempranillo, Cabernet, Syrah; Malvar, Albillo Real, Airén
appellations.summary: Vinos de Madrid covers about 5,900 hectares in four subzones. Arganda (southeast, Tempranillo and Malvar), Navalcarnero (southwest) and El Molar (north, added in 2019) make everyday wine; San Martín de Valdeiglesias, in the foothills of the Sierra de Gredos, makes the stars. There, Comando G (Daniel Jiménez-Landi and Fernando García, with Marc Isart at the start), Bernabeleva, Marañones and 4 Monos make translucent, floral Garnacha from old bush vines on granite, sometimes compared to Burgundy or Châteauneuf.
appellations.terroir: From clay plains near Madrid to granite slopes up to 900 m in the west.
appellations.nerd_note: Comando G's Rumbo al Norte comes from a tiny, north-facing parcel high in the Gredos, one of the highest Garnacha sites in Spain.

appellations.name: Ribera del Guadiana
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Cabernet, Syrah, Merlot; Pardina, Cayetana Blanca, Macabeo, Eva (Beba), Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Extremadura's only DO, with about 41,000 hectares in six subzones: Tierra de Barros (the largest, around Almendralejo), Matanegra, Ribera Alta, Ribera Baja, Montánchez and Cañamero. Mostly a source of value wine, it has a few ambitious producers.
appellations.terroir: Plains of clay (*barros*) and sand, and hilly areas in Cañamero and Montánchez.
appellations.nerd_note: Montánchez has a tradition of *pitarra*, young wine made in earthenware jars.

appellations.name: Dominio de Valdepusa
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Petit Verdot, Graciano
appellations.summary: Spain's first Vino de Pago, the estate of Carlos Falcó, Marqués de Griñón, at Malpica de Tajo in Toledo. Falcó studied at UC Davis, planted Cabernet in 1974 and brought in Richard Smart's canopy-management techniques and drip irrigation. His Syrah and Petit Verdot proved that the La Mancha fringes could make fine wine. Falcó died in 2020; the estate is now run by his children.
appellations.terroir: Clay over limestone in the Tagus valley, at about 450 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Falcó led the campaign for the Vino de Pago category and the Grandeza de España association of single-estate producers.

appellations.name: Finca Élez
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Tempranillo; Chardonnay
appellations.summary: The estate of the film producer Manuel Manzaneque at El Bonillo in Albacete, at about 1,000 m. One of the highest vineyards in Castilla-La Mancha, it became famous for a barrel-fermented Chardonnay.
appellations.terroir: Limestone plateau at 1,000 m with cold nights.
appellations.nerd_note: With Guijoso, it shares the El Bonillo municipality.

appellations.name: Guijoso
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Tempranillo; Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: The pago of the Sánchez Muliterno family at El Bonillo, in the province of Albacete, on a high limestone plateau at about 1,000 m. It was one of the first single-estate pagos after Dominio de Valdepusa. The altitude gives cold nights and slow ripening, so its Chardonnay and Bordeaux-style reds keep a freshness unusual for La Mancha.
appellations.terroir: Stony limestone at about 1,000 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Guijoso and Finca Élez, two pagos in one municipality, show how high (about 1,000 m) the cool fringes of La Mancha reach.

appellations.name: Dehesa del Carrizal
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Merlot, Tempranillo; Chardonnay
appellations.summary: A pago at Retuerta del Bullaque, in the Montes de Toledo (Ciudad Real), on a former hunting estate at about 900 m between oak woodland and the Cabañeros National Park. Planted with Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Merlot, Petit Verdot, Tempranillo and Chardonnay, it shows how the mountains on the northern edge of La Mancha give fresher wines than the plain.
appellations.terroir: Slate and clay hills in the Montes de Toledo.
appellations.nerd_note: It shares its municipality with Vallegarcía, another pago.

appellations.name: Campo de La Guardia
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Petit Verdot, Malbec; Chardonnay
appellations.summary: The pago of Bodegas Martúe in La Guardia, in the province of Toledo, on the plateau between Madrid and the heart of La Mancha. Its stony limestone soils and continental climate give Tempranillo and Bordeaux varieties grown organically on a single estate. Martúe is a member of the Unión de Vinos de Pago.
appellations.terroir: Chalky limestone soils at about 700 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Martúe is a member of the Unión de Vinos de Pago.

appellations.name: Pago Florentino
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo (Cencibel), Syrah, Petit Verdot
appellations.summary: The Castilla-La Mancha pago of the Arzuaga family, best known for their Ribera del Duero winery, at Malagón in Ciudad Real, set among Mediterranean woodland at the foot of the Montes de Toledo. Its rules allow only Tempranillo, Syrah and Petit Verdot, and the estate makes a single red from stony soils at about 650 m.
appellations.terroir: Stony soils at about 650 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Named after Florentino Arzuaga, founder of the family's Ribera winery.

appellations.name: Casa del Blanco
appellations.grapes: Cabernet, Merlot, Syrah, Petit Verdot, Tempranillo; Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: A pago at Manzanares, in the south of the La Mancha plain (Ciudad Real), with alluvial soils on an old river terrace. Its rules allow an unusually wide range of grapes, from local Airén to Cabernet Franc, Malbec, Petit Verdot and Chardonnay, and the estate makes reds and whites under the Pago Casa del Blanco name.
appellations.terroir: Alluvial soils with high magnesium.
appellations.nerd_note: Casa del Blanco is a member of the Unión de Vinos de Pago, the association of single-estate pagos.

appellations.name: Calzadilla
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Cabernet, Syrah
appellations.summary: One of Spain's smallest pagos, about 13 hectares at Huete in the Alcarria hills of Cuenca, where limestone and gypsum soils sit at about 900 m. Its reds blend Tempranillo, Garnacha, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah grown in the hills, an unexpected landscape in the province better known for the plains of La Mancha.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and gypsum hills at about 900 m.
appellations.nerd_note: At 13 hectares it is one of the smallest pagos in Spain.

appellations.name: El Vicario
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Petit Verdot, Graciano, Garnacha; Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: The pago of Pago del Vicario in the municipality of Ciudad Real, registered by the EU in 2019. The estate grows a wide range of reds and two whites on clay and gravel near the Guadiana and makes red, white and rosé, one of the few single-estate DOPs on the open plain around the provincial capital.
appellations.terroir: Clay and gravel at about 650 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Pago del Vicario is a member of the Unión de Vinos de Pago.

appellations.name: La Jaraba
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Graciano; Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: The pago of the Pago de la Jaraba family winery at El Provencio, in the province of Cuenca on the eastern La Mancha plain. Registered by the EU in 2019, it makes reds from Tempranillo, Cabernet, Merlot and Graciano and a Sauvignon Blanc, from limestone and clay at about 700 m.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and clay at about 700 m.
appellations.nerd_note: La Jaraba is a member of the Unión de Vinos de Pago.

appellations.name: Los Cerrillos
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Petit Verdot; Chardonnay
appellations.summary: The pago of Bodegas Montalvo Wilmot at Argamasilla de Alba, in Ciudad Real, registered by the EU in 2019. The town is traditionally identified as the 'place in La Mancha' whose name Cervantes did not want to remember, and the estate makes Tempranillo-led reds and Chardonnay on limestone and red clay.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and red clay on the La Mancha plain.
appellations.nerd_note: Argamasilla de Alba is traditionally identified as the 'village in La Mancha' whose name Cervantes did not want to remember.

appellations.name: Vallegarcía
appellations.grapes: Syrah, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot; Viognier
appellations.summary: A pago at Retuerta del Bullaque in the Montes de Toledo (Ciudad Real), on a large estate at about 850 m that shares its municipality with Dehesa del Carrizal. It made its name with Syrah and with Viognier, one of the first planted in Spain, and Bordeaux-style reds.
appellations.terroir: Slate and clay at about 850 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Its Viognier was among the first in Spain.

appellations.name: Río Negro
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Tinto Fragoso, Syrah, Cabernet, Merlot; Gewürztraminer
appellations.summary: Registered by the EU in March 2025, Río Negro covers just over 470 hectares in Cogolludo, San Andrés and Membrillera in Guadalajara, with the only winery in the delimited area. Its rules list Tinto Fragoso, a native red variety, and a white from 100 percent Gewürztraminer.
appellations.terroir: Hills in northern Guadalajara, toward the Sierra de Ayllón.
appellations.nerd_note: It was the 105th Spanish DOP and the 24th in Castilla-La Mancha.

appellations.name: Rosalejo
appellations.grapes: Varieties not documented in the sources consulted
appellations.summary: Registered in March 2024, Rosalejo is one of Spain's newest pagos. The Ministry of Agriculture's 2023/24 report lists it with 1,338.7 hectares of land and one winery, but no wine marketed during its first campaign. Grape varieties and producer details were not available in the sources consulted.
appellations.terroir: Castilla-La Mancha.
appellations.nerd_note: The ministry recorded no wine marketed under Rosalejo in its first campaign.

appellations.name: El Terrerazo
appellations.grapes: Bobal, Tempranillo, Garnacha, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah
appellations.summary: Toni Sarrión's Mustiguillo estate near Utiel, the first Vino de Pago in the Valencian Community, and the place where Bobal was first proven as a fine wine (Mestizaje, Finca Terrerazo, Quincha Corral).
appellations.terroir: Limestone and clay at about 800 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Sarrión also rescued Merseguera for his white Mestizaje Blanco.

appellations.name: Los Balagueses
appellations.grapes: Syrah, Merlot, Tempranillo; Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: A pago of Bodegas Vegalfaro in the municipality of Requena, on the Utiel-Requena plateau at about 750 m. Unusually for the area it does not include Bobal: its rules allow Syrah, Merlot, Tempranillo, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc. At about 18 hectares it is one of the smallest pagos, shared by two registered wineries in 2023/24.
appellations.terroir: Plateau at about 750 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Vegalfaro is a member of the Unión de Vinos de Pago.

appellations.name: Chozas Carrascal
appellations.grapes: Bobal, Tempranillo, Garnacha, Cabernet, Syrah, Monastrell; Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Macabeo
appellations.summary: The López-Peidro family estate at San Antonio de Requena, farmed organically on the Utiel-Requena plateau at about 700 m. Its rules cover a long list of grapes, from Bobal and Monastrell to Cabernet Franc and Chardonnay, and the estate makes still wines and traditional-method sparkling wines under the pago name.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and clay at about 700 m.
appellations.nerd_note: It makes both still and sparkling wines under the same pago name.

appellations.name: Vera de Estenas
appellations.grapes: Bobal, Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot; Chardonnay
appellations.summary: The Martínez Bermell family estate at Utiel, one of the first in the area to bottle Bobal-based wines, registered as a pago by the EU in 2019. Its clay and limestone soils at about 750 m give Bobal and Tempranillo reds and a Chardonnay; with El Terrerazo, it shows how Utiel's plateau has turned from bulk wine to estate wine.
appellations.terroir: Clay and limestone at about 750 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Vera de Estenas is a member of the Unión de Vinos de Pago.

appellations.name: Tharsys
appellations.grapes: Bobal and other reds; whites and sparkling
appellations.summary: Spain's newest Vino de Pago (EU, October 2025), near Requena. The historic estate was revived in 1998 under its original name, and its pago rules cover quality sparkling wine as well as still red, white and rosé.
appellations.terroir: Requena plateau, limestone and clay.
appellations.nerd_note: With Tharsys, Spain counted 28 Vinos de Pago.

appellations.name: Jerez-Xérès-Sherry / Jerez / Xérès / Sherry
appellations.grapes: Palomino Fino, Pedro Ximénez, Moscatel de Alejandría; historic Beba, Perruno, Vigiriega and others since 2021
appellations.summary:
Sherry is Spain's greatest gift to wine and one of the most misunderstood wines in the world. From a neutral grape (Palomino) grown on white albariza soils near the Atlantic, the bodegas of Jerez, El Puerto and Sanlúcar make a whole family of styles through two kinds of ageing: biological, under a veil of yeast (flor) that keeps the wine pale, dry and sharp, and oxidative, in contact with air, which makes it amber, nutty and rich. A fino is one of the driest, most savoury wines on earth; a 30-year-old palo cortado or oloroso one of the most complex; a PX, made from raisined grapes, so sweet and dense it can be poured over ice cream. And all are made in soleras, fractional blending systems in which wines decades old feed the young.

The production zone covers ten municipalities in Cádiz and Seville, with about 7,000 hectares of vineyard (7,027 in 2022). In 2023/24 Jerez marketed almost 18 million litres. Its main markets are Spain, the UK, the Netherlands, Germany and the US. Sales today are a fraction of their 1970s peak, but quality has never been higher, helped by *en rama* bottlings, rare almacenista and single-cask wines, VOS and VORS certified old wines, and a new generation of growers bottling single pagos.

The 2021 reform, the largest since the DO began, let wines age anywhere in the zone (in force from October 2022), allowed pago names on labels (85 percent rule), brought back historic grape varieties, created Fino Viejo and Manzanilla Pasada categories for wines over seven years old, and opened the door to unfortified Sherry, wines that reach the 15 percent needed for flor naturally, aged at least two years. Some of these major changes needed EU approval and came into use in stages.
appellations.terroir: Albariza (chalky marl with diatom and radiolarian fossils) dominates the best pagos north and west of Jerez: Macharnudo, Carrascal, Balbaína, Añina, Los Tercios. It retains winter rain and forms a crust in summer. The climate is hot (summer highs often above 35 degrees) but tempered by the humid Atlantic poniente, with about 600 mm of rain falling mostly in winter. The hot dry levante wind is the enemy of flor.
appellations.nerd_note: Valdespino's Inocente is one of the very few finos still fermented in barrel, from a single pago (Macharnudo Alto) and aged through ten criaderas.

appellations.name: Manzanilla-Sanlúcar de Barrameda / Manzanilla
appellations.grapes: Palomino Fino (only)
appellations.summary:
Manzanilla is fino's coastal twin, a biologically aged dry wine that must be aged in the bodegas of Sanlúcar de Barrameda, where the Guadalquivir meets the Atlantic opposite the Doñana marshes. The humidity there keeps the flor thick and alive all year, so manzanilla is lighter, fresher and saltier than fino, with notes of chamomile (*manzanilla* in Spanish, though the name may come from the village of Manzanilla in Huelva), green apple, bread dough and sea air. It is the most-drunk Sherry style in Spain, served chilled with prawns, fried fish and jamón.

The DO shares its vineyard and its Consejo Regulador with Jerez. In 2023/24 it marketed about 6 million litres. Its houses are some of the oldest in the region: Delgado Zuleta (1744), Hidalgo La Gitana (1792), Barbadillo (1821). *Manzanilla Pasada*, an older manzanilla with a slightly richer, nuttier edge, now must have at least seven years. Since the 2020s the Consejo has also proposed an unfortified manzanilla, as climate change now often brings Palomino to 15 percent naturally.
appellations.terroir: The Sanlúcar side of the Marco has some of its best albariza pagos, Miraflores, Maína, Balbaína, Callejuela, Martín Miguel and Pastrana, close to the sea. The town's bodegas, especially in the lower town near the river, are humid and cool, ideal for flor.
producers: La Guita (Hijos de Rainera Pérez Marín)
appellations.nerd_note: Bodegas in Sanlúcar's lower town (*barrio bajo*) near the river give a different manzanilla from those in the upper town (*barrio alto*): the closer to the river, the thicker the flor.

appellations.name: Montilla-Moriles
appellations.grapes: Pedro Ximénez (dominant), Airén (Lairén), Moscatel, Baladí, Torrontés, Verdejo, Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
Montilla-Moriles, south of Córdoba, makes the same family of solera-aged wines as Jerez, fino, amontillado, oloroso, palo cortado and PX, but from Pedro Ximénez grown in a hotter, inland climate. The difference matters: Pedro Ximénez here ripens to 15 percent or more naturally, so the finos and many other wines need no fortification at all. Montilla finos are softer, rounder and less salty than those of Jerez, and its sweet PX, from grapes dried in the sun on mats (*paseras*), are the benchmark of the style: Alvear, Toro Albalá and Pérez Barquero keep soleras over a century old.

Historically, Montilla's wines were sold to Jerez to sweeten or blend; the word *amontillado* means 'in the style of Montilla'. The DO, with about 4,300 hectares, also makes fermented young wines in earthenware *tinajas*, and its superior zones, Sierra de Montilla and Moriles Altos, have the best albero (albariza) soils.
appellations.terroir: The Campiña of Córdoba, hot and continental (40 degrees in summer), with albariza soils (*albero*) in the best areas and sandy soils elsewhere.
appellations.nerd_note: Amontillado is literally 'Montilla-style': it was the name Jerez gave to finos that had aged on into an amber, nutty style like the wines of Montilla.

appellations.name: Málaga
appellations.grapes: Moscatel de Alejandría, Moscatel Morisco (Moscatel de grano menudo), Pedro Ximénez
appellations.summary: Málaga was one of Europe's most famous wines from the 17th to the 19th century, a sweet, dark wine known in England as 'Mountain' and loved from London to St Petersburg. In 1878 phylloxera was found near Málaga, the first case in Spain, and the vineyards never fully recovered. The DO covers sweet and fortified wines: *Málaga Dulce*, made from sun-dried Moscatel or PX, with or without fortification and aged for years (Pálido, Noble, Añejo, Trasañejo), *Lágrima* (free-run must), and naturally sweet *vino dulce natural*. In 2001 a sister DO, Sierras de Málaga, was created for dry wines, and the two share a Consejo Regulador.
appellations.terroir: Two zones: the Axarquía, east of the city, on steep slate slopes between the sea and the mountains, with Moscatel; and the Montes de Málaga, north of the city. Grapes are dried on *paseras* in the sun.
appellations.nerd_note: The Axarquía's raisin-drying paseras are recognised by the FAO as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System.

appellations.name: Sierras de Málaga
appellations.grapes: Moscatel, Pedro Ximénez, Chardonnay, Doradilla; Tempranillo, Syrah, Merlot, Cabernet, Petit Verdot, Romé
appellations.summary: Sierras de Málaga covers dry wines from the province's mountains, with the subzone Serranía de Ronda as its star. Around Ronda, at 600 to 1,000 m, a wave of estates since the 1990s, led by the German Friedrich Schatz, Descalzos Viejos, Cortijo Los Aguilares and Bodega Joaquín Fernández, has shown that the mountains can make fresh reds from Pinot Noir, Petit Verdot and local Romé. In the Axarquía, Telmo Rodríguez and Jorge Ordóñez make dry Moscatel.
appellations.terroir: Mountain slopes of slate, clay and limestone; Ronda's continental-Mediterranean climate has cold winters and cool nights.
appellations.nerd_note: Descalzos Viejos's winery is built in a 16th-century Trinitarian convent below Ronda's famous gorge.

appellations.name: Condado de Huelva
appellations.grapes: Zalema (local), Palomino, Listán de Huelva, Garrido Fino, Moscatel, Pedro Ximénez
appellations.summary: Condado de Huelva, between Seville and the Portuguese border near the Doñana marshes, has made wine since Roman times and has a Columbus legend: its wines are said to have sailed on his voyages from nearby Palos de la Frontera and Moguer. It makes young whites from the local Zalema and Sherry-style wines: *Condado Pálido* (biologically aged) and *Condado Viejo* (oxidative), plus sweet wines.
appellations.terroir: Flat land of clay, loam and sand near the Atlantic and the Doñana marshes; hot summers moderated by sea air.
appellations.nerd_note: Zalema, the local white, is almost unknown outside Huelva.

appellations.name: Granada
appellations.grapes: Tempranillo, Garnacha, Syrah, Cabernet, Merlot, Pinot Noir; Vijiriego, Moscatel, Pedro Ximénez, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: Granada covers vineyards at some of Spain's highest altitudes, up to about 1,300 m in the Alpujarra and Contraviesa on the southern slopes of the Sierra Nevada. Local *vino de la costa* was a rosado-like field blend; today a few producers make fresh whites from Vijiriego and Moscatel and reds from Tempranillo and Syrah.
appellations.terroir: High slopes of slate and schist with Mediterranean influence from the sea and mountain coolness.
appellations.nerd_note: Barranco Oscuro in Cádiar claims some of the highest vineyards in Europe, at about 1,300 m.

appellations.name: Lebrija
appellations.grapes: Palomino, Moscatel, Vijiriega, Sauvignon Blanc; Tintilla de Rota
appellations.summary: A tiny Vino de Calidad in the Seville town of Lebrija, which also belongs to the Jerez production zone. It covers wines of the town not made as Sherry: still whites, biologically aged *Lebrija viejo*, and sweet wines. Only one winery was active in 2023/24.
appellations.terroir: Albariza and clay on the edge of the Guadalquivir marshes.
appellations.nerd_note: Lebrija's tradition of 'vino de la tierra' predates the Sherry ageing rules that kept it outside the Jerez name.

appellations.name: Lanzarote
appellations.grapes: Malvasía Volcánica (dominant), Listán Blanco, Diego (Vijariego), Moscatel; Listán Negro, Negramoll
appellations.summary:
Lanzarote's vineyards are a work of land art. After the Timanfaya eruptions of 1730 to 1736 buried the island's farms under black volcanic ash (*picón*), farmers dug funnel-shaped pits (*hoyos*), some several metres deep, down to the old soil, planted a vine at the bottom and built a low semicircular stone wall (*zoco*) on the windward side. The ash acts as a mulch, trapping night dew in a place with almost no rain. La Geria, the most spectacular area, is a protected landscape of thousands of hoyos.

Malvasía Volcánica, a local crossing of Malvasía and Marmajuelo, gives fresh, saline dry whites and the traditional sweet Malvasía. Bodegas El Grifo, founded in 1775, is one of the oldest wineries in the Canaries; Los Bermejos, Stratvs and Puro Rofe lead the modern scene.
appellations.terroir: Black volcanic ash (picón) over older red soil, near-zero rainfall (about 150 mm), strong trade winds.
appellations.nerd_note: Each hoyo usually holds just one to three vines, giving La Geria one of the lowest planting densities of any vineyard in the world.

appellations.name: Tacoronte-Acentejo
appellations.grapes: Listán Negro, Negramoll, Listán Blanco, Malvasía, Vijariego, Castellana Negra
appellations.summary: The first Canary Island DO (1992), on the northeast slopes of Tenerife between Tacoronte and La Matanza, the most planted area of the island. Its reds from Listán Negro and Negramoll, often made by carbonic maceration, are juicy and peppery. The Casa del Vino de Tenerife, in El Sauzal, is the island's wine museum.
appellations.terroir: North-facing volcanic slopes at 100 to 1,000 m, with trade-wind clouds and relatively high rainfall.
appellations.nerd_note: Tacoronte-Acentejo was the first Canary DO, recognised in 1992, a few years before the rest of the islands followed.

appellations.name: Valle de la Orotava
appellations.grapes: Listán Negro, Listán Blanco, Negramoll, Malvasía, Tintilla, Baboso, Vijariego
appellations.summary: The Orotava valley, below Mount Teide on Tenerife's north coast, is home to a unique vine-training system, the *cordón trenzado* (braided cordon): long canes of old ungrafted Listán vines are braided together into horizontal ropes up to 10 metres long, propped on sticks, and a new cane is added each year. Suertes del Marqués, Envínate and Tajinaste have made the valley's mineral, smoky Listán Negro and Listán Blanco famous.
appellations.terroir: North-facing slopes from 250 to 800 m, volcanic soils of ash and lava, trade-wind clouds.
appellations.nerd_note: Because each year's new cane is braided into the old cordon, a cordón trenzado vine is a living record of its own growth, and many are well over a century old.

appellations.name: Ycoden-Daute-Isora
appellations.grapes: Listán Blanco, Malvasía, Vijariego, Marmajuelo; Listán Negro, Negramoll, Tintilla
appellations.summary: On Tenerife's northwest, from Icod de los Vinos and Garachico to Guía de Isora, this DO was the heart of the 16th and 17th century Canary sack trade. Garachico's harbour, from which wine was exported to England, was buried by lava in 1706. Today it makes fresh whites from Listán Blanco and Malvasía.
appellations.terroir: Volcanic slopes from sea level to 1,400 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Icod de los Vinos takes its name from wine and is home to the famous Drago Milenario dragon tree.

appellations.name: Valle de Güímar
appellations.grapes: Listán Blanco, Malvasía, Moscatel, Gual; Listán Negro
appellations.summary: On the east coast of Tenerife, south of Santa Cruz, vines rise to about 1,500 m on volcanic soils, some of the highest vineyards in Europe. Listán Blanco makes most of the wine.
appellations.terroir: East-facing slopes from 200 to 1,500 m, sheltered from trade winds, with pumice and ash soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Some of Güímar's vineyards, at up to 1,500 m, are among the highest in Europe.

appellations.name: Abona
appellations.grapes: Listán Blanco, Malvasía, Albillo Criollo, Vijariego; Listán Negro, Baboso, Tintilla
appellations.summary: Abona, on Tenerife's sunny south, has the highest vineyards in Spain and among the highest in Europe, around Vilaflor at up to about 1,700 m, where old Listán Blanco grows on pumice (*jable*) and volcanic sand. Borja Pérez and Envínate have shown its potential.
appellations.terroir: South-facing slopes from 300 to 1,700 m, sunny and dry, with pumice and sandy volcanic soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Vilaflor de Chasna, at about 1,400 m, is one of Spain's highest villages, with vines planted above it.

appellations.name: La Palma
appellations.grapes: Malvasía Aromática, Listán Blanco, Albillo Criollo, Bujariego (Vijariego); Negramoll, Listán Negro
appellations.summary: La Palma has three subzones: Fuencaliente in the volcanic south, home of sweet Malvasía; Hoyo de Mazo in the east; and the cool north, where *vino de tea* is aged in barrels of Canary pine (*tea*), which gives a resinous flavour. The 2021 Cumbre Vieja eruption damaged vineyards and wineries on the west of the island.
appellations.terroir: Volcanic soils from fresh ash to old weathered clays; altitudes up to 1,500 m.
appellations.nerd_note: *Vino de tea* is a living relic of the days when the islands had no oak, so barrels were made of resinous Canary pine heartwood.

appellations.name: El Hierro
appellations.grapes: Vijariego, Listán Blanco, Verdello; Baboso, Listán Negro, Vijariego Negro
appellations.summary: The westernmost and smallest DO of the Canaries, on the island of El Hierro, with vineyards around the El Golfo valley (Frontera). Baboso Negro, a dark and spicy red, and Vijariego are its signatures.
appellations.terroir: Volcanic slopes from sea level to 700 m.
appellations.nerd_note: El Hierro was once the reference meridian for world maps, the edge of the Old World.

appellations.name: La Gomera
appellations.grapes: Forastera Blanca (Gomera), Listán Blanco, Marmajuelo; Listán Negro, Negramoll
appellations.summary: A small DO on the steep, ravine-cut island of La Gomera, where Forastera Blanca, a local white, grows on tiny terraces. About 125 hectares and 20 wineries.
appellations.terroir: Steep ravines and terraces from 300 to 1,000 m.
appellations.nerd_note: La Gomera's terraced ravines were once cultivated almost to the summit.

appellations.name: Gran Canaria
appellations.grapes: Listán Negro, Negramoll, Tintilla, Vijariego Negro; Listán Blanco, Malvasía, Moscatel
appellations.summary: The DO merged the island's earlier Monte Lentiscal DO in 2005. Its historic vineyards are around the Caldera de Bandama, a volcanic crater near Las Palmas, where the 'vino del Monte' was famous.
appellations.terroir: Volcanic soils from sea level to 1,500 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Bandama's crater has a farm with vines on its floor, 200 m below the rim.

appellations.name: Islas Canarias
match: Vino de Calidad de las Islas Canarias
appellations.grapes: All Canary varieties
appellations.summary: A regional designation created in 2011 covering all the islands, allowing blends across islands and DOs. It is used by producers who source from several islands or make wines outside the rules of their island's DO. The ministry lists it as a Vino de Calidad.
appellations.terroir: All Canary volcanic terroirs.
appellations.nerd_note: Several of the islands' most famous modern wines are labelled Islas Canarias rather than their local DO.

appellations.name: Binissalem
appellations.grapes: Manto Negro (at least 30% in reds), Callet, Cabernet, Syrah, Merlot; Prensal Blanc (Moll), Chardonnay, Moscatel
appellations.summary: Mallorca's first DO, in the centre of the island at the foot of the Serra de Tramuntana, around Binissalem, Santa Maria del Camí and Consell. Manto Negro gives light, fragrant reds. José L. Ferrer, founded in 1931, is the leading house.
appellations.terroir: Calcareous soils with red clay and stones, sheltered by the Tramuntana mountains.
appellations.nerd_note: Manto Negro must make up at least 30 percent of a Binissalem red, a rule that protects the island's native grape.

appellations.name: Pla i Llevant
appellations.grapes: Callet, Manto Negro, Fogoneu, Cabernet, Syrah, Merlot; Prensal Blanc, Parellada, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Pla i Llevant covers the plain (Pla) and eastern (Llevant) parts of Mallorca, around Felanitx, Manacor and Petra. Ànima Negra, founded in Felanitx in 1994, built its reputation on Callet, the island's dark, aromatic native red, and made Mallorca a name in wine.
appellations.terroir: Calcareous red clay and limestone soils, Mediterranean climate.
appellations.nerd_note: Ànima Negra's AN and Son Negre are mostly Callet, a grape once dismissed as only good for blending.

sites.name: Barrio de la Estación, Haro
sites.text: Haro's railway station opened in 1863, and in the phylloxera years the land beside it filled with bodegas that could load wine straight onto trains for Bilbao and Bordeaux. López de Heredia, CVNE, La Rioja Alta, Muga, Bodegas Bilbaínas, Gómez Cruzado, Roda and Ramón Bilbao nearby make it the densest cluster of historic wineries in the world, perhaps. Every June the Barrio stages its own open-door weekend, a pilgrimage for Rioja lovers.

sites.name: R. López de Heredia Viña Tondonia
sites.text: Founded in 1877 by Rafael López de Heredia, the most traditional house in Rioja. Its cellars run deep into the rock beside the Ebro, its barrels are made and repaired by its own coopers, and its Viña Tondonia, Bosconia, Cubillo and Gravonia wines spend years in old American oak. The whites and rosado Gran Reserva are cult wines. The modern tasting pavilion by Zaha Hadid wraps an Art Nouveau stand from the 1910 Brussels fair.

sites.name: Viña Tondonia vineyard
sites.text: A 100-hectare estate on a meander of the Ebro, planted by Rafael López de Heredia on the north bank opposite Haro in the 1910s. Its clay-limestone and alluvial soils supply both the red and white Viña Tondonia, released only after six or more years of barrel ageing and, for the Gran Reservas, decades. One of the few historic Rioja brands named after a real vineyard.

sites.name: CVNE (Compañía Vinícola del Norte de España)
sites.text: Founded in 1879 by the Real de Asúa brothers, CVNE (often spoken as Cune) makes the Imperial Gran Reserva and the Viña Real wines. Its 1909 barrel hall, roofed by a column-free steel truss attributed to the Eiffel engineering firm, remains a landmark of Haro's station quarter. Imperial Gran Reserva 2004 was Wine Spectator's wine of the year in 2013.

sites.name: La Rioja Alta S.A.
sites.text: Founded in 1890 by five families from Rioja and the Basque Country, La Rioja Alta is the guardian of the classic style: long ageing in American oak barrels made in its own cooperage, racked by hand by candlelight. Its Gran Reserva 890 and 904 (named after the founding year, 1890, and the 1904 merger with Bodegas Ardanza) are reference wines for traditional Rioja. The group also owns Torre de Oña in Rioja Alavesa.

sites.name: Bodegas Muga
sites.text: Founded in 1932 by Isaac Muga and Aurora Caño and moved to the station quarter in 1971. Muga ferments in large oak vats, ages in its own barrels and keeps a team of coopers who build and repair both 225-litre barricas and big wooden tinas, a rarity today. It makes both the traditional Prado Enea Gran Reserva and the modern Torre Muga and Aro.

sites.name: Bodegas Roda
sites.text: Founded in 1987 by Mario Rotllant and Carmen Daurella, Roda built its modern cellar on a cliff above the Ebro next to the station quarter. It works with old-vine Tempranillo from selected vineyards around Haro and the Sonsierra, and its research into clones and its Roda I and Cirsion wines helped define the modern Rioja of the 1990s.

sites.name: Bodegas Bilbaínas
sites.text: Founded in 1901 by a Bilbao merchant family on the site of an earlier French-owned wine trading house, Bodegas Bilbaínas holds one of Rioja's largest estates around Haro and underground galleries under the station quarter.
